# `Q-2-45` — Reference-style links are not supported

> `[label][ref]` is reference-style link syntax, which quarto-markdown
> does not support — `[...]` is reserved for span syntax.

## What this means

Pandoc and CommonMark let you write a link in two pieces: a use site
that names a label, and a definition elsewhere that supplies the URL.

```markdown
See [the RedHat documentation][gcc-toolset].

[gcc-toolset]: https://docs.redhat.com/...
```

quarto-markdown has no such syntax. `[...]` is the bracket half of
**span syntax** — `[text]{.class}` — so `[the RedHat documentation]`
and `[gcc-toolset]` are read as two separate spans that happen to sit
next to each other. Neither carries an attribute block, so both render
as bare `<span>` elements and the brackets are discarded:

```html
<p>See <span>the RedHat documentation</span><span>gcc-toolset</span>.</p>
```

The reader sees "See the RedHat documentationgcc-toolset." — no link,
and the label run together with the reference name.

The same applies to images. `![alt][ref]` produces an `<img>` with an
**empty `src`**, which is a broken image rather than merely missing
text.

## Why this happens

Almost always a document written for Pandoc or another Markdown
dialect, or one converted from a source that prefers reference style
for readability — long URLs collected at the bottom of the file.

All three reference forms produce this error:

```markdown
[label][ref]     <!-- full -->
[label][]        <!-- collapsed -->
[ref]            <!-- shortcut (only when a definition exists) -->
```

## How to fix

Move the URL to the use site:

```markdown
See [the RedHat documentation](https://docs.redhat.com/...).
```

then delete the now-unused definition line, which would otherwise
render as visible text (see [`Q-2-46`](Q-2-46.qmd)).

`qmd-syntax-helper` does both automatically:

```bash
# See what would change
qmd-syntax-helper check -r reference-links "docs/**/*.qmd"

# Apply
qmd-syntax-helper convert -r reference-links --in-place "docs/**/*.qmd"
```

It carries titles over, percent-encodes anything the inline form
cannot express, and drops each definition once its last use is gone.
